entities.summary: Pope Lucius II, born Gherardo Caccianemici dal Orso, was head of the Catholic Church and ruler of the Papal States from 9 March 1144 to his death in 1145. His pontificate was notable for the unrest in Rome associated with the Commune of Rome and its attempts to wrest control of the city from the papacy. He supported Empress Matilda's claim to the Kingdom of England in the Anarchy, and had a tense relationship with King Roger II of Sicily. Lucius II was a religious figures from Bologna (1050, Bologna–1145-02-22). Recognized as a landmark figure with global significance (referenced in 0 Wikipedia editions).

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Pope Lucius II's pontificate was marked by unrest in Rome and tensions with Empress Matilda and King Roger II, reflecting broader power struggles during the Anarchy. His support for Matilda's claim to England had lasting regional implications.
